_source: Merged from claude-harness settings/permissions-deny.snippet.json and settings/git-hygiene.snippet.json on 2026-09-02. The rules are documented in claude-harness docs/git-hygiene.md; the project-specific TIGHTENING below is documented in AGENTS.md, which is where rule 13 says they belong.
_ss2_tightening: SUPERSEDED 2026-09-26 (see _ss2_push_refspec): main and master are no longer push-denied here; force-pushes and branch deletion still are. SS2 USED TO TIGHTEN RULE 7, AND NO LONGER DOES. `Bash(git push *)` was in ASK, not allowed, because AGENTS.md said 'Ask before pushing anything' — this repository derives its fixtures from a licensed game, so what leaves the machine was treated as the owner's call rather than a convenience. DROPPED BY THE OWNER 2026-09-12, in chat and at the approval screen, explicitly asking that pushing no longer prompt. So the project is back to harness rule 7 (push feature branches freely) and `Bash(git push *)` is in ALLOW. WHAT STILL BINDS, and it is the part that carried the actual safety: DENY beats everything, so `main`, `master`, `--force`, `-f` and `--force-with-lease` are blocked outright and no allow entry can reach them. Nothing is DENIED that has a legitimate form: a first draft also denied pushes to the working branch, which would have blocked work the owner had explicitly authorised. ONE THING TO WATCH, stated rather than asserted: `Bash(git push --delete *)` and `Bash(git push origin --delete *)` are still in ASK, and this project has NOT measured whether a broad ALLOW entry wins over a narrower ASK one in this build. If a remote-branch deletion ever runs without prompting, move those two entries into DENY — do not assume the ASK held. (The `_ss2_workflow` field below records what it cost the last time this file asserted an unmeasured precedence claim.)
_rule_14_no_verify: The twelve `--no-verify` / `-n` DENY entries are claude-harness settings/git-hygiene.snippet.json's, kept in step with it (the owner's decision, 2026-09-24): nothing may skip the grilling gate's commit-msg hook. Combined short flags (`-an`), abbreviations (`--no-veri`) and `-c core.hooksPath=...` are not matched; CI re-checks every commit. A `-m` message containing ` -n ` is denied too, which this repository's `git commit -F <file>` convention already avoids.
_ss2_workflow: `Workflow` IS IN ASK AGAIN — RE-ADDED BY THE OWNER 2026-09-24, in chat ("fulfill the requests that you could not auto accept from the agent on the remote machine and need my word for"), on a peer session’s request (workflow-audit-44, "Options and recommendations"): it is the ADR 0001 layer that makes the owner approve each wave launch, and every other repository that adopted the ADR 0001 set carries it. HISTORY: it was DROPPED by the owner 2026-09-09 on the reasoning that the dialog bought VISIBILITY, not safety — the deterministic guard is the 6-questions/6-verifiers hard cap inside .claude/workflows/question-fanout-audit.js — and that reasoning is not withdrawn: the cap and the ONE-WAVE-AT-A-TIME rule in AGENTS.md still bind, and a session still states a wave’s spawn count in the transcript before launching it. The dialog is now IN ADDITION to them. NOTE ON AN OLD CLAIM: this field once asserted that bypass-permissions mode skips ASK rules by design; the owner reported being prompted WHILE bypass was active, so that was never true here — test it rather than citing this file.
_ss2_push_refspec: DROPPED BY THE OWNER 2026-09-26, in chat: "drop SS2’s block on pushing main". SS2 had kept the main/master push denies as a recorded TIGHTENING after claude-harness moved them out of its floor into the optional settings/git-hygiene.tighten-main.snippet.json (0aaea22: agents push main and merge their own PRs; the floor denies only what makes history unrecoverable). With this, SS2 is at the harness floor for pushes: force-pushes in any spelling and deleting main/master stay DENIED, and GitHub branch protection on main blocks force-pushes and deletion too. So an agent now fast-forwards main itself after a merge. What was here before, kept for the record: ADDED 2026-09-24, ON THE OWNER’S WORD ("Proceed with what your recommendations are"), WHILE PLANNING HIS FAST-FORWARD OF main: `Bash(git push * main)` matches only a command whose LAST word is `main`, so the refspec forms that actually move main — `git push github arena/champion-capture:main`, `HEAD:refs/heads/main` — and a trailing flag (`git push github main --dry-run`) were not covered by any deny entry. The six entries above close those forms for main and master. MEASURED 2026-09-24 for ONE form: `git push github --dry-run arena/champion-capture:main 2>&1` was DENIED by `Bash(git push *:main)` (a dry-run pushes nothing, so the probe is safe either way). The other five forms are not measured. By the matcher’s design (Claude Code permissions docs, per a peer session) nothing here catches `git -C <dir> push …`, `git -c k=v push …` or a push through `sh -c`: a deny rule is not a security boundary. The owner moved main once from a session on 2026-09-24 (362859a..a89704c), on his explicit word, by lifting this one entry for that push and restoring it. Moving main is the OWNER’s act (git-hygiene rule 11), typed by him, e.g. `! git push github arena/champion-capture:main` — a plain push, which refuses anything but a fast-forward. PARITY WITH THE HARNESS, 2026-09-24, on the owner’s word ("you have permission for the git-c push forms the other machine asked for"): every deny entry of claude-harness main’s settings/git-hygiene.snippet.json (after its PR #2) is now here too — the `git * push …` forms that catch `git -C <dir> push`, and the `…:main *` / `…:refs/heads/main *` refspec-with-options forms, for main and master, plus `git * push --force/-f/--force-with-lease`. Still no glob catches `git -c k=v push`, a quoted `git push`, `sh -c`, or git by path: a deny rule is not a security boundary.
